title: Power Apps: form fill assistance using Microsoft 365 files in model-driven apps
summary: Hold: the legacy environment path is presented as usable although Microsoft now describes those settings as removed from that page. The maker-side path also starts inside the app designer without explaining how to reach it; the roadmap facts, licensing statements and toolbar API are supported.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to extend form fill assistance to use Microsoft 365 files as a source for form entries.
claims.quote: We’re expanding form fill assistance in Power Apps to use Microsoft 365 files as a source, helping users turn existing content into form entries with less manual effort.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development"

claims.claim: The roadmap lists General Availability and Preview release phases.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.claim: The roadmap product is Power Apps.
claims.quote: "products": ["Power Apps"]

claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant).
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.claim: The roadmap platforms are Android, iOS and Web.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Android", "iOS", "Web"]

claims.claim: The roadmap target is January CY2027.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "January CY2027"

claims.claim: The roadmap preview date is October CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "October CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap availability table lists the Monthly release channel.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; What's changing; Open questions
claims.claim: The default state on arrival of the Microsoft 365 files extension is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: "form fill assistance" "default" "Microsoft 365" files. Read roadmap, form-filling-assistance, settings-features and powerapps-flow-licensing-faq; existing-feature defaults are documented, but no extension-specific arrival default was found.

claims.claim: The documented form fill assistance licensing model is per-user.
claims.quote: The form fill assistance requires specific user licenses based on the product.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Form fill assistance in Power Apps model-driven apps requires a Power Apps premium licence.
claims.quote: Power Apps model-driven app: The user must have a Power Apps premium license.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Form fill assistance in Dynamics 365 model-driven apps requires a Dynamics 365 enterprise or premium licence.
claims.quote: Dynamics 365 model-driven app: The user must have a Dynamics 365 enterprise or premium license as outlined in Dynamics 365 License Guide.

claims.claim: Users without the required licence do not see the feature.
claims.quote: If the user doesn't have the license, the feature is hidden.

claims.claim: Licence enforcement gradually rolls out following general availability.
claims.quote: This license enforcement gradually rolls out following the feature's general availability.

claims.claim: Learn describes current form fill assistance as generally available in Dynamics 365 apps.
claims.quote: This feature is generally available in Dynamics 365 apps.

claims.claim: Learn describes current form fill assistance as production-ready preview in Power Apps.
claims.quote: This feature is in production ready preview in Power Apps.

claims.claim: Current form fill suggestions can be based on app usage.
claims.quote: Based on the user's usage of the app, what information is already available in the form, and their frequently used data.

claims.claim: Current form fill suggestions can use smart paste as a source.
claims.quote: Based on the copied text the user provides through the Smart paste capability.

claims.claim: Current form fill suggestions can use user-provided files as a source.
claims.quote: Based on the file contents the user provides through the Files capability.

claims.claim: The current files capability supports txt, docx, csv, pdf and image files.
claims.quote: Supported file types are .txt, .docx, .csv, .pdf, .png, .jpg, .jpeg, and .bmp.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: The current files capability does not support files classified with sensitivity labels.
claims.quote: Files classified with sensitivity labels aren't supported.

claims.where: What's changing; Open questions: sensitivity labels
claims.claim: Microsoft has not confirmed that current file limits and sensitivity-label behaviour describe the Microsoft 365 files extension.
claims.quote: Searched: "form fill assistance" "Microsoft 365 files" default licensing source locations permissions sensitivity labels. Opened form-filling-assistance and its FAQ; they describe user-provided files and a separate Copilot chat experience, not this extension's final limits.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented the Microsoft 365 files extension's file-access boundaries.
claims.quote: Searched: "form fill assistance" "Microsoft 365 files" default licensing source locations permissions sensitivity labels; "Microsoft 365 files" "form" "Power Apps". Read form-filling-assistance and its FAQ; no file-access boundaries for the roadmap extension were found.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Suggestions are not saved until the user accepts them.
claims.quote: Suggestions are entirely optional and aren't saved in the app until you accept them.

claims.claim: AI suggestions require user review for accuracy and appropriateness.
claims.quote: Users should ensure these suggestions are accurate and appropriate before accepting them.

claims.claim: Fields with column security are not currently supported.
claims.quote: Fields that have column security aren't currently supported.

claims.claim: Usage may be throttled.
claims.quote: Usage might be subject to service limits or throttling. Microsoft reserves the right to update the limits.

claims.claim: An additional charge specific to the Microsoft 365 files source is not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: "form fill assistance" "Microsoft 365 files" pricing credits charge license. Opened form-filling-assistance and powerapps-flow-licensing-faq, including its form-fill licensing section; no additional charge specific to this source was found.

claims.claim: The documented current form fill experience is available in web apps with the modern look enabled.
claims.quote: Form fill assistance is available for all apps on the web where the modern, refreshed look is turned on.

claims.claim: The Allow form fill assistance column property must be enabled for the affected column.
claims.quote: The Allow form fill assistance column property enabled for the column where form fill assistance occurs.

claims.claim: The environment form fill control is reached in Power Platform admin center through Copilot > Settings > Power Apps > Data entry.
claims.quote: The primary admin control for form fill assistance is moving to the Power Platform admin center under Copilot > Settings > Power Apps > Data entry.

claims.claim: An API for the Copilot Data entry control is not documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: "form fill assistance" "Data entry" Power Platform API PowerShell pac admin; site:learn.microsoft.com/power-platform "API" "data entry agent". Read Copilot hub, pac admin, PowerShell support and Environment Management Settings update reference; no mapped control API found.

claims.claim: The legacy environment switch remains reachable through Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > AI form fill assistance.
claims.quote: The following settings are removed from the Environment > Settings > Features page. Access them through Manage model-driven app settings in the app designer or Solution Explorer App Settings.
claims.fix: Remove the legacy environment switch row from both controls and the rendered table. Its cited page now says those settings are removed from the environment Features page; retain the separately documented Copilot Data entry and app toolbar rows.

claims.claim: No API is documented for the legacy environment switch as the row names it.
claims.quote: Searched: "form fill assistance" environment settings PowerShell API PowerAppsFormPredict; "FormPredictSmartPasteEnabled" "FormFileUploadEnabled" environment SaveSettingValue. Read settings-features, client API and environment settings update reference; no API for the named legacy switch found.

claims.claim: Administration is moving from the legacy environment Features page to Copilot settings.
claims.quote: Admin controls for the AI form fill assistance feature are changing. The primary admin control moves to Copilot > Settings > Power Apps > Data entry.

claims.claim: The maker-side route is App designer > Settings > Features > Form fill assist toolbar.
claims.quote: Select Solutions. ... Choose the solution that contains the model-driven app where editing is required. ... On the left navigation pane select Apps, select a model-driven app, and then on the toolbar select Edit.
claims.fix: Replace the path in controls[2].ui and the table with 'Solutions > solution > Apps > app > Edit > Settings > Features > Form fill assist toolbar'. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/maker/model-driven-apps/create-edit-app for entering the designer, retaining app-properties for the setting itself.

claims.where: controls[2].api; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: saveSettingValue("FormFileUploadEnabled", true, { overrideScope: 2, solutionUniqueName: "<solution>" }) sets the current app's toolbar setting.
claims.quote: Xrm.Utility.getGlobalContext().saveSettingValue(settingName, value, saveSettingOptions).then(successCallback, errorCallback); ... Use 2 to add or update a setting app value.

claims.claim: Designer setting changes require saving and publishing the app.
claims.quote: You must select Publish to activate an app settings change. ... Save and Publish the app.

claims.claim: No separate UI or API switch specific to Microsoft 365 files as a source is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "form fill assistance" "Microsoft 365 files" admin settings API switch. Opened form-filling-assistance, settings-features, app-properties and Copilot hub; found general form-fill and toolbar controls, not a source-specific switch.

claims.claim: Makers can configure Allow form fill assistance (preview) per column.
claims.quote: Allow form fill assistance (preview) ... When enabled, users receive suggestions generated by AI for columns that support form fill assistance in main and quick create forms.

claims.claim: The per-column property is the finest-grained control.
claims.quote: Searched: "form fill assistance" "column" "granular". Opened create-edit-field-portal, form-filling-assistance, app-properties and Copilot hub; they document column and broader settings but do not state that no finer-grained control exists.
claims.fix: Remove 'which is the finest-grained control and the one to use for sensitive fields' and replace it with 'and disable it for columns that might contain sensitive information'.

claims.claim: The column property can be disabled for columns that might contain sensitive information.
claims.quote: You can disable for columns that might contain sensitive information, such as email address.

claims.claim: The Power Platform admin center Copilot area reports usage for the data entry agent.
claims.quote: Admins can view usage analytics for the data entry agent and data exploration agent on the Power Apps page to understand the value that end users are getting from AI in Power Apps.

claims.claim: Supported Microsoft 365 file locations for the roadmap extension remain undocumented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Microsoft 365 files" "form" "Power Apps"; "form fill assistance" "Microsoft 365 files" default licensing source locations permissions sensitivity labels. Read form-filling-assistance and its FAQ; no extension-specific supported-location list found.

claims.claim: Licensing specific to the Microsoft 365 files extension has not yet been published.
claims.quote: Searched: "form fill assistance" "Microsoft 365 files" pricing credits charge license. Read the feature licensing section and Power Platform licensing FAQs; they document existing user licences but do not identify a licence specific to the new source.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The checklist directs readers to review column properties, but the controls table has no column-property row.
claims.quote: Review environment form fill settings and column properties. ... Table rows cover environment Data entry, the legacy environment switch, the app toolbar and a Microsoft 365 files source switch, but not column properties.
claims.fix: Remove 'and column properties' from the checklist step, leaving 'Review environment form fill settings.' Do not add a control row.
